Look up a journal specification

Source: R/journal_specs.R
journal_spec.Rd

Every size, limit, and style rule in OlinkViz comes from one registry of journal specifications: column widths, the maximum figure height, the smallest (and, where a guide states one, largest) text size, the minimum stroke weight, the panel-tag style, and the raster resolution the journal asks for. [journal_width()], [save_olinkviz()], [olinkviz_combine()], [theme_journal()] and the `olinkviz_check_*()` pre-flight checks all read it.

Usage

journal_spec(journal = "nature")

Arguments

journal

A registered journal id (see [journal_specs()]; matching is case-insensitive), or a spec object, which is returned unchanged.

Value

An object of class `olinkviz_journal_spec`: a list with `id`, `name`, `publisher`, `kind`, `widths_mm` (named column widths: `minimal`, `single`, `onehalf`, `double`, `triple`), `widths_alt_mm` (alternative widths a publisher quotes elsewhere), `grid` (2 or 3 columns), `max_height_mm`, `font`, `font_min_pt`, `font_max_pt`, `body_pt`, `line_min_pt`, `tag_case`, `tag_pt`, `dpi` (`line`, `halftone`, `combination`), `formats`, `colour`, `checked`, `verified`, `sources`, `notes` and `filled`. `NA` means the guide does not state the value.

Details

The registry holds

- **hand-checked presets**: `"nature"`, `"cell"` and `"science"` (read from each publisher's own figure pages), `"natcomms"`, `"pnas"`, `"plos"`, `"jid"`, and a journal-agnostic `"default"` (90 / 180 mm, at most 240 mm tall, 7 pt minimum text, 300 dpi); - **researched presets** for 53 further journals and publishers (dermatology, allergy, microbiome, bioinformatics, pharmacology, statistics, general medicine) compiled from each author guide, with the source URLs and the date checked. Where a guide does not state a value it was filled from the publisher's generic artwork guide or a package default; those fields are listed in `$filled` and starred by `print()`; - **purpose presets** (`"slides"`, `"poster"`, `"thesis"`, `"grant"`, `"preprint"`, `"web"`) that are house conventions, not journal rules; - anything you add with [journal_spec_add()].

Author guidelines change and several journals deviate from their publisher's flagship rules: re-check the live guide of your target journal before final submission. Each spec's `$verified`, `$checked` and `$sources` say how far to trust it.

See also

Other journal-specs: journal_font(), journal_height(), journal_spec_add(), journal_specs(), journal_width()

Examples

journal_spec("nature")
#> <journal spec> nature: Nature (Springer Nature) [journal]
#>   widths      single 90 | 1.5 120 | double 180 mm  (also quoted: 89 / 183 mm)
#>   max height  170 mm
#>   text        5-7 pt (body 7 pt)
#>   lines       not stated *
#>   panel tags  lower-case, 8 pt bold
#>   raster dpi  halftone >= 300
#>   fonts       Arial, Helvetica
#>   formats     PDF, EPS, AI
#>   colour      RGB
#>   provenance  publisher page, checked 2026-10
#>               https://research-figure-guide.nature.com/figures/building-and-exporting-figure-panels/
#>               https://research-figure-guide.nature.com/figures/preparing-figures-our-specifications/
#>   * not stated by the guide:
#>       line_min_pt: none stated; checks use 0.25 pt
#>   notes:
#>     Text must be 5-7 pt at final size (guide: 'Minimum text size: 5 pt', 'Maximum
#>     text size: 7 pt'); panel labels are 8-pt bold, upright, lower-case; the
#>     maximum figure height is 170 mm. Nature's figure guide quotes 89 / 183 mm
#>     columns while its author formatting guide quotes 90 / 180 mm: 90 / 180 is
#>     used here and 89 / 183 is accepted as an alternative. The 120 mm
#>     one-and-a-half column is the Nature Portfolio convention, not a
#>     flagship-Nature number. A 7 pt 'minimum' sometimes quoted for Nature is its
#>     maximum text size.
journal_spec("cell")$max_height_mm
#> [1] 200
journal_spec("science")$widths_mm
#>  single onehalf  double 
#>      57     121     184
